summary: Halenor's storm isles: the wreck-right, wreckers or wayfinders, first of the isles, the storm fleet and the war at sea.

wreck_right.name: The Wreck-Right
wreck_right.desc: What the storm throws on the shore belongs to the sea-lords. It is an old right, and a profitable one, and no honest man in Halenor will say how often the storm has been helped.

storm_crown.name: The Storm Crown
storm_crown.desc: The four isles of Halenor have one crown at last, a ring of black driftwood set with a single grey pearl. It is worn by the first among equals, and it is passed on at sea.

wreckers.name: Wreckers of the Storm Isles
wreckers.desc: Lamps are lit on the cliffs on the nights the gales blow in. By morning the shore is littered with cargo, and no one saw a thing.

storm_pilots.name: Wayfinders of the Storms
storm_pilots.desc: The old wreckers who turned to piloting know where every rock lies and which gale is real. A ship with a Halenor wayfinder aboard sails in weather others will not face.

corsair_harbours.name: The Corsair Harbours
corsair_harbours.desc: Every cove of the four isles has a quay, a warehouse and no questions. Raiders sell their prizes here and keep their boats in the dry sheds over winter.

isles_protector.name: The Isles' Protector
isles_protector.desc: Halenor guards the smaller isles with its fleet and expects them to remember it. The lesser harbours fly the sea-lord's flag beside their own.

storm_riders.name: Ships That Ride the Storm
storm_riders.desc: The storm fleet puts to sea in weather that sends other fleets to harbour. Its hulls are heavy, its crews are tough and its captains do not read the omens.

storm_sea_soldiers.name: Sea Soldiers of the Storm
storm_sea_soldiers.desc: Islanders who have clung to oars in a gale find a hard march no great trial. They are strong, wet, and happy to hit something.

storm_isles_apart.name: The Storm Isles Keep Apart
storm_isles_apart.desc: Whatever the great crowns do, the four isles stay in their harbours with the gales at their backs. The sea-lords have told their captains so.

protection_offer.title: Halenor Offers Its Protection
protection_offer.desc: A black-sailed galley has come into our harbour with a sea-lord in the bow. Halenor will guard our waters against corsairs, he says, and our fishers will be safe under the Storm Lords' shield. His men are courteous, and his galleys are many.

focuses.name: The Sea-Lords' Hall
focuses.desc: Halenor is four isles under the rule of its sea-lords, who meet under Orvak Halen in a hall roofed with the keels of old wrecks. Each lord brings a ship and a grievance.

focuses.name: The Four Isles
focuses.desc: The sea-lords walk the bounds of their four isles, and draw them on a single map. Every cove, rock and wrecking-shore is named, and every name has an owner.

focuses.name: Orvak's Oath
focuses.desc: Orvak Halen swears the oldest of oaths to his sea-lords: that no lord shall take what is another's, and no wreck shall be shared out unfairly. Old Gull, keeper of the wreck-right, stands witness.

focuses.name: The Storm Crown
focuses.desc: The first among the sea-lords is crowned in a gale, on a rock that the surf covers twice a day. The crown is black driftwood, and he must keep it dry.

focuses.name: The Wreck-Right
focuses.desc: The sea-lords have claimed the wreck-right since their grandfathers' time. The question now is whether to keep it as a trade, or to turn it into something safer.

focuses.name: Wreckers of the Storm Isles
focuses.desc: The old wreckers' trade is revived: false lights on the headlands, boats waiting in the lee, and no survivors who will talk. It pays well, and it ends badly.

focuses.name: Wayfinders of the Storms
focuses.desc: The sea-lords turn their storm-lore to better use. Their best captains learn to guide ships through the gales that have wrecked so many, and to charge a fair price for it.

focuses.name: False Lights
focuses.desc: Lamps on the cliffs are swung to show a safe passage that is not there. Every captain in the Pupor knows the trick, and some still sail in.

focuses.name: Wayfinders for Hire
focuses.desc: Halenor's wayfinders sail aboard merchant ships for a fixed fee. They take a tenth of the cargo's value, and they are worth every coin.

focuses.name: The Corsair Harbours
focuses.desc: Halenor opens its coves to any raider with silver. The sea-lords take a share of every prize and ask no questions about the flag.

focuses.name: Wayfinders for the West
focuses.desc: The western fleets must cross the central sea, and Halenor knows its storms. The sea-lords offer their best wayfinders to the Ford Council for a price.

focuses.name: First of the Isles
focuses.desc: Halenor has more men than any other island realm, and its sea-lords have begun to speak as if the other isles were their cousins. Not all of the cousins agree.

focuses.name: Envoys to the Lesser Isles
focuses.desc: Sea-lords in long cloaks travel to the smaller isles with an offer of protection. They are courteous, they are armed, and they do not ask twice.

focuses.name: The Isles' Protector
focuses.desc: Halenor's fleet takes the lesser harbours under its wing and keeps the corsairs off them. The lesser harbours fly its flag beside their own, and some of them mean it.

focuses.name: The Isles by the Sword
focuses.desc: The sea-lords have asked politely, and politely again. If the lesser isles will not take the shield, they will be given it with the sword.

focuses.name: A Crown Over the Isles
focuses.desc: With three realms under its flag, Halenor claims the old title of sea-king. The crown is made from the copper of three wrecked flagships.

focuses.name: The Storm Yards
focuses.desc: Slips are cut into the lee of the main isle, where the cliffs break the worst of the gales. The hulls built here are thick-planked and slow to sink.

focuses.name: Storm Galleys
focuses.desc: The yard-masters learn to build a galley with a high bow and a deep keel. It rows heavily, but it does not roll.

focuses.name: The Storm Fleet
focuses.desc: Rhea Stormwake has sailed through more gales than any captain in the isles. The sea-lords give her the first fleet to be raised under the Storm Crown.

focuses.name: Ships That Ride the Storm
focuses.desc: The fleet sails out in the worst weather of the year and returns with every ship afloat. The crews have learned what the sea can do, and have stopped being afraid of it.

focuses.name: Island Raiders
focuses.desc: The biggest galleys of the storm fleet are fitted for boarding, with grapnels, rams and covered decks. They fight best where the sea is roughest.

focuses.name: Harbours of Halenor
focuses.desc: Piers and breakwaters are built in the best of the four isles' coves. A ship that comes to Halenor in a gale may now find a berth.

focuses.name: Salvage Yards
focuses.desc: The wreck-right is made into a trade. Wrecks are surveyed, stripped and sold at fixed prices by the salvage-masters, and not a plank is wasted.

focuses.name: The Storm Markets
focuses.desc: Traders from the lesser isles bring their wares to a market held between storms. Whatever the weather has left unbroken is for sale.

focuses.name: Rope, Tar and Timber
focuses.desc: Driftwood is sawn into planks and hemp is spun into rope. The isles buy less from abroad, and their ships are better for it.

focuses.name: The Isle Levy
focuses.desc: Every sea-lord musters the men of his isle once a year. They are fishers and wreckers, and they fight with oar and hatchet.

focuses.name: Sea Soldiers of the Storm
focuses.desc: The levy is drilled to fight from boats, wade ashore and form a shield-wall in the surf. They are not elegant, and they do not need to be.

focuses.name: Bows of the Isles
focuses.desc: The islanders string their bows with sealskin and wax them against the wet. They shoot from a pitching deck better than most men shoot on land.

focuses.name: The Storm Host
focuses.desc: The levy of the four isles is drawn up in one host. The sea-lords review it on the beach, in the rain, and none of the men complain.

focuses.name: The War at Sea
focuses.desc: The great fleets of the mainland have taken to the water, and the storm isles lie in their path. The sea-lords meet in the dark, with the wind shouting at the shutters.

focuses.name: The Storm Isles Keep Apart
focuses.desc: The sea-lords vote to keep their galleys in harbour and their hands off the quarrel. Halenor has its own storms to weather, and wants no others.

focuses.name: Wayfinders for the Crossing
focuses.desc: The western host will cross a sea that Halenor knows too well. The sea-lords sell their wayfinders to the Crossing, and wish them luck.

focuses.name: Storm Wayfinders for the Living
focuses.desc: The stranger who sailed north once begged a wayfinder from the storm isles, and the sea-lords have not forgotten. They send their best to join the coalition.
